answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded identity with a per-identity cost floor. Before acting, an agent must post collateral that is slashed if its identity is caught voting with clones. Cheap identity creation stops paying: every thousand sybils needs a thousand bonds, tying up capital a single fraud verdict can burn. The ledger trusts only a signal from a bond that cleared a waiting period, so burst-registered accounts cannot harbor hidden duplicates. Like a willow needing real roots before it resists wind, trust is earned slowly and priced honestly.
